# Second Album

Follow-up to "Two Roads" (2023). Tracking at Riverstone Audio, sessions begin Oct 3 2026.

## Quartet
- Jessica Webb, tenor and alto
- Ray Coleman, piano
- Luke Vance, bass
- Tomoko Ishida, drums

## Working tracklist
1. Crossroads (new, in sketch)
2. Two Roads Reprise
3. Westport Morning
4. For Frank (ballad)
5. one more uptempo to write

## Open items
- [ ] Lock tracklist with Ray
- [ ] Book Riverstone for October
- [ ] Decide on a horn guest for one track
- [ ] Talk budget with Gloria

# Memoir Draft

Working title: "Two Roads" (same as the record, may change).

About growing up between two worlds in Kansas City. Dad's jazz records and Sunday rehearsals on one side, Mom's quiet Sundays on the other. Learning the horn at Heartland Conservatory.

## Chapters in progress
- The Record Cabinet
- First Horn
- Crossroads (how the school started)
- Two Roads (the album, the title)

## Notes
- Keep it honest, not nostalgic
- Ruth Reichl's food writing is the tone I want
- [ ] Ask Mom about the Jacksonville years

# HSU-KC Guest Lectures

Fall 2026, HSU-KC jazz program

Coordinating with Tomoko on a 3-session guest series:
- Session 1: Building a small-ensemble sound, Jessica Webb
- Session 2: Improvisation and the language of the blues, open
- Session 3: Artist Q&A and open rehearsal

## Status
- Tomoko confirmed program interest (Mar 2026)
- Dates pending the fall academic calendar

# Crossroads (Sketch)

New tune for the second album, probably the opener.

## Form
- Intro: rubato sax over a piano pedal
- Head: 32 bars, AABA
- Solos: sax, then piano, trade fours with Tomoko
- Out head, tag the last 4

## Notes
- Key: D minor, modal feel on the A sections, the bridge moves to F
- Tempo: medium, around 132
- Named for the school and the neighborhood, and the obvious double meaning
- [ ] Write the real bridge melody, only have a rough idea so far

# Two Roads Reprise (Sketch)

A shorter reharmonized take on the title track from the first record, to close the new album.

## Idea
- Same melody, slower, half-time feel
- Reharm the turnaround with more color tones
- Just sax and piano for the first chorus, full quartet on the second
- End unaccompanied, long tone fade

## Notes
- Key: B flat, drops to G for the reprise feel
- Around 4 minutes
- Ray likes the duo opening, keep it

# A Love Supreme, Listening Notes

Coltrane, 1965. Still the north star.

## What I keep stealing
- The four-note cell in Acknowledgement, how it moves through every key
- Elvin's elastic time, never rushes
- Tyner's left hand, those quartal voicings
- Resolution: the melody is a prayer, so play it like one

## For teaching
- Use Acknowledgement to show motivic development to the advanced ensemble
- Pairs with the memoir chapter on Dad's records, this was one of his

- idea: a horn guest on the album, maybe call Frank to ask who
- ask Gloria about the Roth contribution for the quarter
